name: Galvanized Horn
summary: A Galvanized Horn is a hardened biological growth harvested from the formidable chimaera matriarchs haunting the scorched crags of Kalimdor. Highly sought after by master armorers across both factions, this resilient specimen serves as a core material for specialized warrior armor.

sections.title: Trophy of the Charred Vale
sections.body: Chimaeras are savage, twin-headed beasts known for their ferocity, but the elder matriarchs that prowl the Charred Vale in the Stonetalon Mountains bear horns forged unusually hard by ash, flame, and survival. While standard fledglings yield brittle, blackened horns, the matriarch's horn possesses a naturally tempered strength akin to treated metal. Both the dwarven armorer Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and Orm Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff covet the horn, requiring it as a test of martial valor and as a critical ingredient in crafting exceptional mail armor.

faq.q: Where does a Galvanized Horn come from?
faq.answer: It is taken from chimaera matriarchs residing in the Charred Vale, located in the southwestern reaches of the Stonetalon Mountains.

faq.q: Why do smiths want this specific horn?
faq.answer: Master armorers prize the horn for its natural density and heat-resistant properties, using it to reinforce specialized suits of mail and plate armor.

For Alliance warriors, Furen Longbeard in Stormwind demands the horn to forge fire-hardened armor. For Horde warriors, Orm Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff seeks it as proof of strength to fashion a warrior's helm.

faq.q: How does it differ from a regular Charred Horn?
aliases: is it different from charred horn
faq.answer: Common charred horns are easily gathered from lesser, fledgling chimaeras. The galvanized horn comes exclusively from a mature matriarch, possessing a far denser, tempered structure suitable for masterwork smithing.

angles.text: Slaying a matriarch and securing her galvanized horn is a trial of endurance and power, proving a warrior's mettle to master armorers in Stormwind or Thunder Bluff.
The horn demonstrates how organic materials hardened in extreme environments can match or exceed worked metals in custom armor reinforcement.
